statement: Let a preprocessing choice be any subsequence S of nums, obtained by deleting zero or more entries while preserving order; S may be empty. For an integer t with 0 <= t <= len(queries), call t processable if there is a preprocessing choice S and, for each s = 0,1,...,t-1, a choice of either the first or the last element of the current sequence such that: initially the current sequence is S; at step s the current sequence is nonempty, the chosen side's element is at least queries[s], and that element is removed. The function returns r and r is the largest processable t. It does not fail.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(queries) >= 1, len(nums) <= 1000, len(queries) <= 1000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), nums[i] is an integer with 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^9, and for every j with 0 <= j < len(queries), queries[j] is an integer with 1 <= queries[j] <= 10^9.

statement: The function returns a result r; it does not fail.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(queries) >= 1, len(nums) <= 1000, len(queries) <= 1000, and all nums[i] and queries[j] are in [1, 10^9].

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, we have 0 <= r <= min(len(nums), len(queries)).
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(queries) >= 1, len(nums) <= 1000, len(queries) <= 1000, and all nums[i] and queries[j] are in [1, 10^9].

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 0 if and only if for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), nums[i] < queries[0].
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(queries) >= 1, len(nums) <= 1000, len(queries) <= 1000, and all nums[i] and queries[j] are in [1, 10^9].

statement: Let c = nums[0]. The function returns r = 1 if c >= queries[0], and r = 0 otherwise.
preconditions: len(nums) = 1, len(queries) >= 1, len(queries) <= 1000, nums[0] is in [1, 10^9], and all queries[j] are in [1, 10^9].

statement: The function returns r = min(len(nums), len(queries)).
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(queries) >= 1, len(nums) <= 1000, len(queries) <= 1000, all nums[i] and queries[j] are in [1, 10^9], and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and every j with 0 <= j < len(queries), nums[i] >= queries[j].

statement: Let p be the least integer with 0 <= p <= len(queries) such that either p = len(queries) or queries[p] > c. Then the function returns r = min(len(nums), p).
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(queries) >= 1, len(nums) <= 1000, len(queries) <= 1000, all nums[i] and queries[j] are in [1, 10^9], and there is an integer c such that nums[i] = c for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = len(nums) if and only if the first len(nums) queries can be processed starting from the full original slice nums itself with no initial replacement; that is, there exists a sequence of choices of the current first or last element for len(nums) steps such that each chosen element is at least the corresponding query and is removed. Consequently r < len(nums) otherwise.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(queries) >= 1, len(nums) <= len(queries), len(nums) <= 1000, len(queries) <= 1000, and all nums[i] and queries[j] are in [1, 10^9].

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every t with 0 <= t <= r, there exists a preprocessing subsequence S of nums and a sequence of side choices that processes the first t queries.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(queries) >= 1, len(nums) <= 1000, len(queries) <= 1000, and all nums[i] and queries[j] are in [1, 10^9].

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, there exists a preprocessing subsequence S of nums and a sequence of side choices that processes exactly the first r queries.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(queries) >= 1, len(nums) <= 1000, len(queries) <= 1000, and all nums[i] and queries[j] are in [1, 10^9].

statement: Let revnums be the slice of length len(nums) with revnums[i] = nums[len(nums)-1-i] for 0 <= i < len(nums). If maximum_processable_queries(nums, queries) returns r and maximum_processable_queries(revnums, queries) returns r', then r = r'.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(queries) >= 1, len(nums) <= 1000, len(queries) <= 1000, and all nums[i] and queries[j] are in [1, 10^9].

statement: Whenever maximum_processable_queries(nums, queries) returns r and maximum_processable_queries(nums2, queries) returns r2, we have r <= r2.
preconditions: nums and nums2 are slices of lengths at least 1 and at most 1000, len(queries) >= 1 and at most 1000, all entries are in [1, 10^9], and nums is a subsequence of nums2: there exist indices 0 <= j0 < j1 < ... < j(len(nums)-1) < len(nums2) with nums[i] = nums2[ji] for every i.

statement: Whenever maximum_processable_queries(nums, queries) returns r and maximum_processable_queries(nums, queries2) returns r2, we have r >= r2.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(queries) = len(queries2) >= 1, len(nums) <= 1000, len(queries) <= 1000, all entries are in [1, 10^9], and queries[j] <= queries2[j] for every j with 0 <= j < len(queries).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every integer v, the number of indices i with 0 <= i < r and queries[i] > v is at most the number of indices j with 0 <= j < len(nums) and nums[j] > v.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(queries) >= 1, len(nums) <= 1000, len(queries) <= 1000, and all nums[i] and queries[j] are in [1, 10^9].

statement: If maximum_processable_queries(nums, queries) returns r and maximum_processable_queries(nums, Qm) returns rm, then rm = min(r, m).
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(queries) >= 1, len(nums) <= 1000, len(queries) <= 1000, all entries are in [1, 10^9], and 1 <= m <= len(queries). Let Qm be the slice of length m with Qm[j] = queries[j] for 0 <= j < m.
